narrative.overview: A high-contrast editorial register shared with ewancroft.uk. Green-tinted near-black on near-white, Variable Inter set with tight display tracking, JetBrains Mono for the technical register, and surfaces distinguished by tonal value and a hairline border rather than by decoration. This replaces the earlier cool-navy/glassmorphism system: where that reached for translucent headers and app-matched shadows, this one trusts contrast — the page is nearly white, the type is nearly black, and the single green accent is reserved for interactive signals. It feels at home in the AT Protocol ecosystem: technical without being cold, warm without being beige.
keyCharacteristics: High contrast first: body text-900 on background-50, headings text-950, checked against 4.5:1
Typography-first hierarchy: weight, size, and tight tracking do the work; color is secondary
Mono as a technical register: nav, footer, metadata, captions, and section labels speak in JetBrains Mono
Tonal + border surfaces: cards and lists step up via raised surface and a 1px border — no drop shadows anywhere
Single-accent discipline: one green for links, focus rings, markers, and the wordmark dot
Light/dark parity: every color is a light-dark() pair defined once per token
Calm motion: exponential-eased entrances, decisive press feedback, reduced-motion collapse
Ecosystem-native: sits beside the personal site and the AT Protocol ecosystem's indie-web confidence

rules.name: The High-Contrast Rule
rules.body: Body text is text-900 on background-50; headings are text-950. Muted text is text-600, still checked to clear 4.5:1 against background-50. Never place body text on text-700 or lighter.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Accent green appears on links, focus rings, list markers, the active nav underline, and the wordmark dot — as the interactive signal, not as a decorative surface. A primary button is dark (text-950), not green.

rules.name: The Tonal + Border Rule
rules.body: Cards, lists, and callouts differentiate from the page via the raised surface and a 1px border. There are no drop shadows, no gradients, no glass.

rules.name: The Typography-First Rule
rules.body: Visual hierarchy is established through weight, size, and tracking — never through color splashes. If a heading needs a color accent to feel important, the weight or size is wrong.

rules.name: The One Display Rule
rules.body: The hero h1 is the only element at Display weight (800) on any page. Section headings step down to Section Title (700).

rules.name: The No-Glass, No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no box-shadow, no gradients. The sticky nav is a solid background-50 bar with a bottom border — legibility comes from contrast, not blur.

rules.name: The Feedback-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Animation plays on content entrance and on direct manipulation only — never as ambient looping decoration. Entrances use ease-out-expo; interaction uses ease-out-quart.

dos: Do keep body text text-900 on background-50 and headings text-950 — high contrast is the system's signature
Do use the mono register (JetBrains Mono) for nav, footer, metadata, and captions
Do differentiate surfaces with tonal value + a 1px border, never a shadow
Do use text-wrap: balance on headings and text-wrap: pretty on prose
Do cap body text lines at 60–70ch
Do test every color against its background for ≥4.5:1 contrast (body) and ≥3:1 (large text)
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation
Do support both light and dark color schemes via light-dark()
Do reserve the accent green for interactive signals (links, focus, markers, the wordmark dot)
Do trust the reader — the AT Protocol audience is technically literate; state the value clearly without over-explaining
donts: Don't use drop shadows, gradients, or backdrop-filter anywhere — the sticky nav is a solid bar
Don't make a primary button accent-green — primary buttons are text-950/background-50 inverse
Don't use the SaaS startup template kit: no gradient hero backgrounds, no animated metric counters, no glassmorphism
Don't set body text lighter than text-700 against the page background
Don't use position: absolute inside overflow: hidden containers for dropdowns
Don't animate CSS layout properties — use transform and opacity for compositor-only animations
Don't over-explain the AT Protocol to the audience — link to atproto.com for background; the site sells the app, not the protocol
